content.user_title: Manage Arize AI Azure Resources in .NET
content.value_statement: Managing Arize AI organizations through Azure ARM can require several SDK types and async workflows. This skill gives concise .NET guidance for authentication, CRUD operations, listings, updates, deletion, and direct resource access.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install the Azure.ResourceManager.ArizeAIObservabilityEval package.
Explains DefaultAzureCredential and ArmClient setup for Azure SDK clients.
Provides guidance for creating, reading, updating, and deleting Arize AI organizations.
Covers listing organizations by resource group and subscription.
Documents key SDK resource, collection, data, patch, marketplace, user, and SSO types.
Summarizes error handling, long-running operations, retry policies, and direct resource access.
limitations: Does not provision Azure resources without valid Azure permissions and marketplace access.
Does not replace official Azure SDK reference documentation for every API member.
Does not validate real tenant IDs, subscription IDs, marketplace terms, or pricing.
Does not manage non-.NET implementations or Arize services outside this Azure resource provider.

use_cases.title: Provision Arize AI Organizations
use_cases.description: Create Azure Marketplace-managed Arize AI organizations with the correct ARM resource type, location, offer details, and user contact fields.

use_cases.title: Build .NET Resource Management Tools
use_cases.description: Add Arize AI organization management to internal .NET services that already use Azure SDK authentication and ARM clients.

use_cases.title: Operate ML Observability Resources
use_cases.description: List organizations, inspect provisioning state, update tags, and remove retired resources through repeatable Azure SDK workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Install and Authenticate
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new .NET project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to add the Arize AI Observability and Evaluation Azure SDK package to a .NET project and authenticate with DefaultAzureCredential.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Organization
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create an Arize AI organization on Azure using the .NET ARM SDK. Use placeholders for tenant, subscription, resource group, marketplace, and user details.

prompt_templates.title: Manage the Resource Lifecycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a .NET workflow to get, list, update tags, and delete Arize AI organizations with proper async handling and Azure RequestFailedException handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Arize AI Azure resource management flow for retries, long-running operations, least-privilege credentials, direct resource access, and deletion safeguards.

output_examples.input: I need to create an Arize AI organization from a .NET admin service.
output_examples.output: A guided plan covering package setup, Azure SDK authentication, resource group lookup, marketplace details, user contact fields, and long-running operation handling.

output_examples.input: I want to manage existing Arize AI organizations across a subscription.
output_examples.output: A workflow that explains subscription-level listing, resource group operations, existence checks, tag updates, and direct resource access by resource ID.

output_examples.input: I need safer operational guidance for deleting an organization.
output_examples.output: A deletion checklist covering permission checks, confirmation steps, dependency review, async completion handling, and Azure error handling.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential with managed identity or a service principal, and avoid hardcoded secrets.
Handle Azure long-running operations, retries, and RequestFailedException paths explicitly.
Use existence checks and direct resource identifiers to reduce unnecessary listing and exception-driven control flow.
anti_patterns: Pasting real client secrets, tenant IDs, or subscription IDs into prompts or shared examples.
Assuming marketplace offer, plan, term, or subscription identifiers are valid without checking Azure Marketplace requirements.
Deleting Arize AI organizations without confirmation, dependency review, and completion monitoring.

faq.question: What Azure package does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure.ResourceManager.ArizeAIObservabilityEval for managing Arize AI Observability and Evaluation organizations with .NET.

faq.question: Which authentication method does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends DefaultAzureCredential through the Azure SDK, using secure environment, managed identity, or developer credential sources.

faq.question: Can it help create Arize AI organizations?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains the ARM collection, organization data model, marketplace fields, user details, and long-running create operation.

faq.question: Does it support update and delete workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers tag updates, resource lookup, deletion, and error handling patterns for Azure SDK operations.

faq.question: Is this useful outside .NET?
faq.answer: Only indirectly. The examples and type names are specific to the .NET Azure Resource Manager SDK.

faq.question: Should I share real Azure secrets with this skill?
faq.answer: No. Use placeholders in prompts and keep real tenant IDs, client IDs, subscription IDs, and client secrets out of chat history.
